imaging: Findings: Peribronchial cuffing and mild hyperinflation. No focal consolidation, effusion, or pneumothorax. Cardiothymic silhouette normal. Impression: Findings compatible with viral illness/reactive airway disease. No pneumonia.

Findings: Large adenoid soft tissue markedly narrowing the nasopharyngeal airway (adenoid-nasopharyngeal ratio approximately 0.8). Palatine tonsils enlarged. Prevertebral soft tissues normal. Impression: Adenotonsillar hypertrophy.
cardiology: Total sleep time 431 min, sleep efficiency 86%. Obstructive AHI 14.0 events/h (REM AHI 26.3). Central AI 0.9/h. Oxygen saturation nadir 81%; time with SpO2 < 90%: 6% of total sleep time. Peak EtCO2 54 mm Hg; EtCO2 > 50 mm Hg for 9% of TST. Snoring loud, continuous. No arrhythmia (sinus rhythm 72-118). Interpretation: Severe obstructive sleep apnea, pediatric criteria (oAHI >= 10). Recommend ENT evaluation for adenotonsillectomy; postoperative inpatient monitoring given severity and nadir < 85%.
encounters: Discharged home 03/11/2022 on ad lib feeds
Discharged same day after PACU agitation episode
notes: Male infant born 03/02/2022 at 34 0/7 wk by SVD after preterm labor; maternal GBS unknown, received adequate IAP. BW 2,280 g. Apgars 7/9. Admitted NICU for feeding immaturity. Course: room air throughout, no apnea/bradycardia events requiring stimulation, no caffeine. NG gavage feeds advanced, ad lib PO by DOL 7. Bilirubin peak 9.6 DOL 3, no phototherapy. Hearing screen passed bilaterally. Newborn screen normal. HepB given. Car seat challenge passed. Discharge wt 2,260 g. Follow-up with PCP in 2 days.

12-month WCC. Growing well along 25th percentile (corrected). Walking with support, 3 words. Ears: R TM bulging, 3rd AOM this winter, amoxicillin. Vaccines per schedule. Hgb 11.3, lead negative. Anticipatory guidance given.

23-month-old with 7 episodes of AOM in 12 months and bilateral middle ear effusion > 3 months with type B tympanograms. Speech mildly delayed per mother. Plan: bilateral myringotomy and tubes. Tonsils 2+. Mild snoring. Will reassess sleep at follow-up.

Anesthesia record, BMT. ASA 1. Inhalation induction sevoflurane 8% in N2O/O2 by mask, maintenance sevoflurane 2-3% by mask, oral airway. No IV. Case 12 min. Fentanyl 1 mcg/kg intranasal. Ketorolac not given. Uneventful intraop. PACU: severe emergence agitation (PAED 18) x 20 min, inconsolable, thrashing; PIV placed in PACU, propofol 17 mg (1 mg/kg) IV with resolution. Discharged home 1240.

Pt emerged screaming, kicking, not recognizing mother, pulling at monitors. Anesthesia at bedside. PIV 24 g L hand placed. Propofol given per anesthesia. Calm and sleeping in 3 min. SpO2 97% RA. Mother upset; asked that "next time" he get something before waking up. Discharge criteria met 1235.
Post-tube check. Tubes patent bilaterally. Sound field thresholds within normal limits. Speech improving per mother. Return PRN.

2 y 10 mo with 3 days URI, now wheezing and tachypnea. RR 44, SpO2 92% RA, subcostal retractions. Albuterol 2.5 mg neb x 3 and prednisolone 2 mg/kg. After: RR 30, SpO2 96%, scattered end-expiratory wheeze. CXR viral pattern. CBC unremarkable. Discharged with albuterol MDI/spacer and prednisolone x 5 days. Follow up PCP. Dx: reactive airway disease exacerbation with viral URI.

4-year WCC. Wt 16.3 kg (55th %ile), Ht 100 cm. Development appropriate. Mother reports loud snoring, pauses, restless sleep, bedwetting returned, and teacher reports inattention. Tonsils 3+. Albuterol only with colds. Kindergarten boosters given. Vision/hearing screen passed. Plan: ENT referral; consider PSG.

Mother calls: fever 39.2, sore throat, not eating. Seen same day by NP; rapid strep positive. Amoxicillin 50 mg/kg/day x 10 days sent to Walgreens Jefferson City. This is the 3rd tonsillitis episode this year.

Tonsillitis, 5th episode in 2026. Rapid strep positive. Failed amoxicillin in July per mother (fever persisted). Amoxicillin-clavulanate ES x 10 days. Tonsils 4+ with exudate. Already referred to ENT; appt 08/25.

Return visit. 5-6 episodes of tonsillitis in 2026, documented. Snoring with witnessed apneas. Tonsils 4+, kissing. Lateral neck film: large adenoid. Plan: PSG to quantify, then T&A. Discussed postop overnight stay if OSA severe.

Mother: "How did his sleep study go? He barely slept in that room." Reply (Dr. Saldana): Results show severe obstructive sleep apnea. Report sent to Dr. Haddad. Surgery is the usual treatment and he will likely need to stay overnight after surgery.

HPI: 4 y 7 mo boy with loud nightly snoring, witnessed pauses, mouth breathing, restless sleep, daytime behavior problems. 6 episodes of tonsillitis this year. PSG 09/14: oAHI 14, nadir 81%. PMH: born 34 wk, NICU 9 days for feeding, no intubation. RAD, albuterol with colds; last used this month. UTD on vaccines. PSH: BMT 04/2024 mask anesthesia; mother states "emergence agitation, required propofol." Meds: albuterol PRN, fluticasone nasal, cetirizine. NKDA. Exam: Wt 17 kg (60th %ile), Ht 102 cm. Tonsils 4+, kissing. Mouth breathing, hyponasal speech. Lungs: scattered rhonchi, clears with cough. Loose lower front tooth (#O). TMs intact, tubes out. A/P: severe OSA, recurrent tonsillitis. Tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy 10/27, overnight observation with continuous oximetry. Consent obtained from mother. Dexamethasone at induction.

Hi, this is Micah's mom. Before his surgery I wanted to ask something. My brother was stuck on the ventilator for hours after his appendix surgery years ago. They told him he couldn't break down a muscle relaxant. Does Micah need a blood test for that? Also he is getting a little cold, is that ok? Thank you.

Reply to mother: Thank you for letting us know. Please mention this to the anesthesia team on the day of surgery, they will review. For the cold, please call the office if he develops fever. Message routed to: R. Haddad, MD (read 10/21).

Sick visit. Cough and runny nose since 10/19. Tmax 38.1 on 10/20, afebrile since. Persistent wet cough, clear to yellow nasal discharge. Eating less, drinking OK. Exam: T 37.2, RR 24, SpO2 97% RA. Nasal congestion, purulent-appearing rhinorrhea. Tonsils 4+, no exudate. Lungs: coarse breath sounds bilaterally, no wheeze, no retractions. Viral PCR negative for COVID/flu/RSV. A/P: viral URI. No antibiotics. Albuterol PRN. Flu vaccine deferred today. Has T&A scheduled 10/27; OK for surgery if afebrile. Return if worse.

Preop call to mother. Arrival 0545 10/27, Pediatric Surgery entrance. NPO instructions reviewed per pediatric handout: no solid food or milk after midnight; mother states "he usually eats dinner at 7." Clear liquids per handout. Bring albuterol and spacer. Mother reports he still has "a little cough." Child life will meet family in preop. Mother asks if she can come back for "going to sleep"; told anesthesia will discuss.

Met pt and mother in preop. Tablet distraction, mask practice with stickers and scent (bubble gum). Pt clingy and tearful, cries when staff approach, calms with mother. Mother requests to be present for induction. Coping plan shared with anesthesia.
orders: Admit to pediatric observation postop, continuous pulse oximetry
Dexamethasone 8.5 mg IV x1 intraop (0.5 mg/kg)
Acetaminophen 15 mg/kg PO/IV q6h scheduled x 48 h postop
